results.title: 14K MILF fighters await decommissioning
results.description: ABOUT 14,000 former Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) fighters are still awaiting decommissioning, prompting a Bangsamoro civic group to urge President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to meet with MILF Chairman Al Haj Murad Ebrahim to advance the stalled peace process. The Amana coalition said Monday that a meeting between Marcos and Murad before the Bangsamoro Parliament opens on Oct. 30 could help move the peace process toward a final agreement and the completion of the fighters’ transition from armed struggle to civilian life. “Fifty years. Twenty months. One meeting,” said Sultan Alim Saad Amate, the group’s convenor. The group said Murad requested a meeting with Marcos in a letter dated Oct. 1. The group also said no former MILF fighters had undergone decommissioning since July 2024. The proposed meeting would bring together Marcos and the MILF chairman, whose organization is a partner of the government in the Bangsamoro peace agreement. Amana said the meeting could help complete a peace process that began with the signing of the Tripoli Agreement in 1976 under the administration of Marcos’ father, the late president Ferdinand Marcos Sr. The group described a proposed exit agreement as the final step in the process, with the government and the MILF needing to agree on its terms. “Father opened. Son can close,” Amate said. The call comes amid changes in the Bangsamoro leadership following the Sept. 14 elections. In March 2025, Marcos appointed Abdulraof Macacua, a former MILF chief of staff, as interim chief minister in place of Murad. Macacua now leads the Bangsamoro Federalist Party while Murad remains chairman of the MILF. “The seat moved. The command stayed,” Amate said, arguing that the leadership change had not ended the fighters’ allegiance to the MILF chairman. Since the September elections, Marcos has met with Macacua and leaders of the Bangsamoro Grand Coalition, including Basilan Gov. Mujiv Hataman, former Sulu governor Sakur Tan, Lanao del Sur Gov. Mamintal Adiong Jr., and Sulu Vice Gov. Abdusakur Tan. The MILF, however, has yet to be received by Marcos, Amana said. “The table is set. One chair is empty,” Amate said. Amana also endorsed the United Bangsamoro Justice Party’s proposal for a “rainbow coalition” government that would bring together the MILF, Moro National Liberation Front, other elected parties, Indigenous Peoples and settlers. The party, founded by the MILF, won 30 seats in the September elections, including all six elected sectoral seats, according to the group. “Many colors, one Bangsamoro,” said Maulana Mamutuk, Amana’s co-convenor. Mamutuk also cited a September Social Weather Stations survey showing that Marcos’ national net satisfaction rating fell to minus 11, while his rating in Mindanao remained positive. “Mindanao moved first. Now, Malacañang,” he said. Amana urged Marcos to meet Murad before Parliament opens on Oct. 30, saying the meeting could help secure the final chapter of the peace process. “Isang pulong. Isang pirma. Isang pamana (One meeting. One signature. One legacy),” Mamutuk said.
